#!/bin/bash
#flux: --partition=compute-od-gpu
#flux: --job-name=stable-diffusion-512cont-improvedaesthetics
#flux: --nodes=20
#flux: --gpus-per-node=8
#flux: --tasks-per-node=1
#flux: --cpus-per-task=32
#flux: --output=stable-diffusion-512cont-improvedaesthetics_%J.out
# The Slurm directive '--cpus-per-gpu=4' combined with '--gpus-per-node=8' implies a request for
# 32 CPUs per node. This has been translated to '--cpus-per-task=32' as there is only one task per node.
# The Slurm output format '%x_%j.%n.out' is not fully supported in Flux. '%x' (job name)
# and '%j' (job ID) are available, but '%n' (node rank) is not. The output filename has been simplified.

# nccl / efa stuff
module load intelmpi
source /opt/intel/mpi/latest/env/vars.sh
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/aws-ofi-nccl/lib:/opt/amazon/efa/lib64:/usr/local/cuda-11.0/efa/lib:/usr/local/cuda-11.0/lib:/usr/local/cuda-11.0/lib64:/usr/local/cuda-11.0:/opt/nccl/build/lib:/opt/aws-ofi-nccl-install/lib:/opt/aws-ofi-nccl/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export NCCL_PROTO=simple
export PATH=/opt/amazon/efa/bin:$PATH
export LD_PRELOAD="/opt/nccl/build/lib/libnccl.so"
export FI_EFA_FORK_SAFE=1
export FI_LOG_LEVEL=1
export FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA=1 # use for p4dn
export NCCL_DEBUG=info
export PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1
export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0
export OMPI_MCA_mtl_base_verbose=1
export FI_EFA_ENABLE_SHM_TRANSFER=0
export FI_PROVIDER=efa
export FI_EFA_TX_MIN_CREDITS=64
export NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD=0

# pytorch multinode vars
# In Flux, we can get the master address by querying the hostname of rank 0.
export MASTER_ADDR=$(flux exec -r 0 hostname)
export MASTER_PORT=11338
export WORLD_SIZE=${FLUX_JOB_NNODES}

echo MASTER_ADDR=${MASTER_ADDR}
echo MASTER_PORT=${MASTER_PORT}
echo WORLD_SIZE=${WORLD_SIZE}

# The 'srun' command is replaced with 'flux run'. It will launch one task on each of the 20 nodes.
flux run bash /fsx/stable-diffusion/stable-diffusion/scripts/slurm/resume_512/launcher.sh

issues: The job directives request a single task per node (`--tasks-per-node=1`) but then launches a `launcher.sh` script. This is a common pattern for multi-GPU training, where the single task on each node is responsible for launching the actual training processes (e.g., one process per GPU). This setup is valid, but it's important to ensure that the `launcher.sh` script correctly starts the 8 local processes to utilize the 8 allocated GPUs on each node.

The script loads an external MPI library (`module load intelmpi`) and then uses `flux run` to launch the application. `flux run` is tightly integrated with Flux's own process management and MPI support. This can lead to runtime conflicts, library mismatches, or other unexpected failures. It is strongly recommended to build and run the application against the MPI implementation provided by or integrated with the Flux environment to ensure compatibility and prevent potential runtime errors.

The job will be allocated a default number of cores (often just one) per task/node. The `launcher.sh` script is expected to start 8 processes to utilize the 8 GPUs on each node. These 8 processes will be forced to share a single CPU core, leading to extreme CPU contention and a severe performance bottleneck. The original job requested 32 CPUs per node, and this omission will cripple the job's performance.

The script loads an external MPI library (`module load intelmpi`) and then uses `flux run` to launch the application. `flux run` is tightly integrated with Flux's own process management and MPI support. This can lead to runtime conflicts, library mismatches, or other unexpected failures. It is strongly recommended to build and run the application against the MPI implementation provided by or integrated with the Flux environment to ensure compatibility.

#SBATCH --job-name=stable-diffusion-512cont-improvedaesthetics
#SBATCH --nodes=20
#SBATCH --gpus-per-node=8
#SBATCH --cpus-per-gpu=4
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --output=%x_%j.%n.out

# nccl / efa stuff
module load intelmpi
source /opt/intel/mpi/latest/env/vars.sh
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/aws-ofi-nccl/lib:/opt/amazon/efa/lib64:/usr/local/cuda-11.0/efa/lib:/usr/local/cuda-11.0/lib:/usr/local/cuda-11.0/lib64:/usr/local/cuda-11.0:/opt/nccl/build/lib:/opt/aws-ofi-nccl-install/lib:/opt/aws-ofi-nccl/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export NCCL_PROTO=simple
export PATH=/opt/amazon/efa/bin:$PATH
export LD_PRELOAD="/opt/nccl/build/lib/libnccl.so"
export FI_EFA_FORK_SAFE=1
export FI_LOG_LEVEL=1
export FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA=1 # use for p4dn
export NCCL_DEBUG=info
export PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1
export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0
export OMPI_MCA_mtl_base_verbose=1
export FI_EFA_ENABLE_SHM_TRANSFER=0
export FI_PROVIDER=efa
export FI_EFA_TX_MIN_CREDITS=64
export NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD=0

# pytorch multinode vars
# node rank should be set in launcher script
export MASTER_ADDR=$(scontrol show hostnames "$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST" | head -n 1)
export MASTER_PORT=11338
export WORLD_SIZE=$(scontrol show hostnames "$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST" | wc -l)

echo MASTER_ADDR=${MASTER_ADDR}
echo MASTER_PORT=${MASTER_PORT}
echo WORLD_SIZE=${WORLD_SIZE}

srun --output=%x_%j.%n.out bash /fsx/stable-diffusion/stable-diffusion/scripts/slurm/resume_512/launcher.sh
